readingInstruction: Read Ezekiel 12:1-14:23. Ezekiel packs his bags to dramatize exile, condemns false prophets who say “Peace,” and exposes idols in the heart. Read especially 14:1-11 and 14:12-23.
settingTheScene: The exiles in Babylon were hearing prophets who told them that the fall of Jerusalem was far off, or would not happen. Ezekiel’s sign-acts and words in these chapters answer them. Chapter 12 shows him leaving his house like an exile. Chapter 13 attacks false prophets and prophetesses. Chapter 14 deals with elders who come to inquire of the LORD while hiding idols in their hearts.
observation: “Son of man, you dwell in the midst of a rebellious house, who have eyes to see, but see not, who have ears to hear, but hear not” (12:2).
“None of my words will be delayed any longer, but the word that I speak will be performed” (12:28).
“Woe to the foolish prophets who follow their own spirit, and have seen nothing!” (13:3).
“They have misled my people, saying, Peace, when there is no peace, and because, when the people build a wall, these prophets smear it with whitewash” (13:10).
“Son of man, these men have taken their idols into their hearts, and set the stumbling block of their iniquity before their faces” (14:3).
“Repent and turn away from your idols, and turn away your faces from all your abominations” (14:6).
“Even if these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they would deliver but their own lives by their righteousness” (14:14).
“I have not done without cause all that I have done in it, declares the Lord GOD” (14:23).
interpretation:
Ezekiel’s sign-act in chapter 12 is an exile’s departure. He packs his baggage in daylight, digs through a wall in the evening, covers his face, and goes out in the dark. It dramatizes what will happen to the prince in Jerusalem: Zedekiah will try to flee through a hole in the wall, and be caught. The people ask, “The vision that he sees is for many days from now.” God says, “None of my words will be delayed any longer.” The false comfort of delay is removed.

Chapter 13 attacks those who profit from false hope. The prophets “prophesy from their own hearts.” They are like jackals in the ruins, not repairing the breach in the wall. They are like those who whitewash a flimsy wall. When the storm comes, it falls. A wall looks solid but cannot stand. The false prophetesses use magic bands to ensnare souls. The common thread is that they lead God’s people away from reality.

Chapter 14 is one of the most searching passages in the Bible. Elders come to Ezekiel to inquire of the LORD. God says that they have idols in their hearts. They are outwardly respectable and inwardly corrupted. “Should I be consulted by them at all?” God will answer such a person himself in a way that will frighten him. The call is to repent. God does not want a religious show but a turned heart.

The chapter ends with four judgments: famine, wild beasts, sword, and plague. Even if Noah, Daniel, and Job were there, they would save only themselves. Righteousness is personal. No one can be saved by the faith of another. Yet there will be survivors, and when they arrive in Babylon, the exiles will see how wicked they were and be comforted. The last line gives God’s reason: “You shall know that I have not done without cause all that I have done.” The judgment is just.
connection: Jesus warned against false prophets in sheep’s clothing (Matthew 7:15) and said, “You are like whitewashed tombs” (Matthew 23:27). 1 John 5:21 says, “Little children, keep yourselves from idols.” Colossians 3:5 says that covetousness is idolatry. 2 Timothy 4:3-4 speaks of teachers who say what itching ears want to hear. James 4:8 says, “Cleanse your hands, you sinners, and purify your hearts.” Romans 14:12: “Each of us will give an account of himself to God.”
application:
Ask: What idol have I taken into my heart? Name it honestly before God.

Are there places in your life where you whitewash a weak wall: appearances, excuses, or comfortable lies?

Be wary of comfort that does not come from the word of God.
prayerPrompts: Ask God to search your heart and show you your idols.
Repent and turn from them in your own words.
Ask him to keep you from false teachers.
